correctness.rationale: For D_p(N)=floor(N/p)-floor(N/(p+1)), membership of p in the floor set is D_p>0 and D_p(N)-D_p(N-1)=1_{p|N}-1_{p+1|N}. Primes <=sqrt(N-1) persist by interval length; for p>=sqrt N D_p values are 0/1. At odd N>=5 the latter p is odd so p+1 cannot divide N. Hence exactly one new prime iff P+(N)>=sqrt N; at odd squares p=sqrt N is counted correctly. Direct independent prime-sieve window computation verified 24998 odd integers 5..49999.

evidence: Heyman Thm 2 for primes and Thm 3 for odd semiprimes; Ma–Wu studies asymptotics.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither asymptotic counting nor these isolated factorizations imply a law for arbitrary odd N.

evidence: Original Conjecture 4 is conditional on three distinct odd primes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new indicator-step argument proves that conjecture and more; this is not implied by the published prime and semiprime special cases.

evidence: Heyman Conjecture 4 gives exactly the three-prime dichotomy.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claimed all-odd step law is strictly stronger; its triple specialization is a direct consequence rather than an equivalent prior theorem.

evidence: OEIS gives the sequence and a fast computational formula; MathDB explicitly lists three-prime problem as open.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A database of values does not prove an all-odd prime-factor threshold.

originality.rationale: Heyman (2021/22) explicitly conjectures the three-distinct-prime case and proves only prime/odd-semiprime cases. This proof establishes the stronger all-odd exact step law. Ma–Wu asymptotic prime counts and OEIS cardinality formulas do not imply exact increments.
residual_risks: Potential later unpublished resolution of Heyman Conjecture 4; MathDB is not a definitive live novelty certificate.
